sections.label: National Vaccination Programme
sections.summary: The National Vaccination Programme was put in place to protect the population from disease through vaccination.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
sentences.text: First, we have put in place the National Vaccination Programme to ensure that the population is well protected from disease through vaccination.

sections.label: Safe management measures implementation
sections.summary: Safe management measures such as limits on group and event sizes, safe distancing and work-from-home arrangements were implemented to keep community cases from overwhelming healthcare capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
sentences.text: Third, we have continued to implement safe management measures (SMMs), such as limits on group and event sizes, safe distancing and work-from-home arrangements, to ensure community cases do not rise out of control and overwhelm our healthcare capacity.

sections.label: Simplifying COVID-19 safe management measures
sections.summary: The Multi-Ministry Taskforce announced plans to simplify and rationalise COVID-19 SMMs to focus on five measures: mask-wearing, group sizes, capacity limits, safe distancing and workplace arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
sentences.text: The Multi-Ministry Taskforce (MTF) had previously announced plans to simplify and rationalise our COVID-19 SMMs to focus on the five most important and effective measures: mask-wearing; group sizes; capacity limits; safe distancing and workplace arrangements.

sections.label: Bill, SMMs and VDS
sections.summary: The Bill, along with SMMs and Vaccination-differentiated Safe Management Measures, allowed quick reaction to Omicron variants without lockdowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill, along with Safe Management Measures (SMMs) and Vaccination-differentiated Safe Management Measures (VDS) have allowed us to react as quickly as we did towards the more infectious Omicron variants, without the need to resort to lockdowns.

sections.label: Extending clauses with trigger points
sections.summary: A question asked whether MOH could extend the clauses for a certain period only if a trigger point such as a rise in the R number or deaths is hit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Rather than this be given carte blanche, can MOH extend the clauses for a certain period of time only if we hit a certain trigger point, for example, if the R number or the number of deaths go up to a certain rate.

sections.label: Nudging unvaccinated individuals
sections.summary: A question asked what plans the Ministry has to nudge remaining unvaccinated individuals, especially those not medically exempted, to get vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share what are the plans to nudge the remaining unvaccinated individuals to get vaccinated, especially those who are not medically exempted?

sections.label: Case numbers and vaccination rates
sections.summary: Official cases exceed 885,000, or 16% of the population, with 91% fully vaccinated and about 69% boosted as at 9 March.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our official case numbers, as of today, stand at more than 885,000, or 16% of the Singapore population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As at 9 March, the MOH reports that 91% has been fully vaccinated, with about 69% having received booster jabs.

sections.label: Move towards normalcy
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill as prudent and says the next year should see Singapore move significantly towards normalcy, with borders reopening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, while I support the Bill as prudent, the next one year should ideally see Singapore continue to move significantly towards normalcy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are promising signs here and elsewhere, with the reopening of international borders, and I note that the Minister for Transport announced this week that Singapore is aiming to restore international air travel through Changi Airport to at least 50% of pre-pandemic levels this year.

sections.label: Unvaccinated share of ICU cases
sections.summary: During the Omicron wave, the 3% of adults partially or unvaccinated contributed 20% of ICU cases and about 30% of mortality.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Even though Omicron causes less severe disease than the Delta strain, during this recent Omicron wave, the 3% of adults who were partially or unvaccinated contributed to 20% of our ICU cases, occupied two-thirds of our ICU beds and caused about 30% or so of the mortality that we see.

sections.label: Unvaccinated Omicron ICU and death risk
sections.summary: Non fully-vaccinated adults infected with Omicron are up to 18 times more likely to end up in ICU and 38 times more likely to die.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Non fully-vaccinated adults infected with Omicron variant, which supposedly is already milder than Delta, are up to 18 times more likely to end up in ICU and 38 times more likely to die from COVID-19 infection, compared to vaccinated and boosted adults.

sections.label: Long COVID risk for unvaccinated
sections.summary: An unvaccinated adult has a one-in-10 chance of getting long COVID-19 after infection, and vaccination reduces this risk significantly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Even for the adult population of all age groups, an unvaccinated person is at risk of a one-in-10 chance of getting long COVID-19 after a COVID-19 infection and it has been proven time and again that vaccination can reduce this risk significantly.

sections.label: Vaccination effectiveness and healthcare system
sections.summary: The situation attests to mRNA vaccine effectiveness and public trust, with adjustments to Protocols 123 and SMMs preventing healthcare system collapse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Such a move would have been unthinkable one-and-a-half years ago and our healthcare system at that time could well have been overwhelmed if the same numbers of daily infections were to be seen at that point.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, this clearly attests to the effectiveness of the mRNA vaccines and the trust and unity of our people in responding to the call to get vaccinated and boosted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Our adjustments to Protocols 123 and the maintenance of some SMMs have allowed us to ride through this wave currently without causing our healthcare system to collapse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In a best-case scenario when COVID-19 ceases to be a threat before the end of 12 months, regulations that are no longer relevant can be repealed and Part 7 can be allowed to lapse.
